Parity validates existence, naming convention, alias nonredundancy, and completeness but cannot validate why an exemption remains appropriate.

candidates.title: Give ESLint cache policy a typed reusable boundary

evidence.note: The shell helper writes its NUL-delimited path input to a temporary file, then embeds a Node program in a heredoc to hash paths and contents.
Cache preparation, stale-directory pruning, and argument construction communicate through ambient MUSI_ESLINT_MAIN_CACHE_DIR and MUSI_ESLINT_MAIN_CACHE_ARGS globals.
The TypeScript consumer constructs inline Bash that sources the shell library, splits stdout into argument lines, and checks only the first token before forwarding the remainder.

candidates.problem: Cache identity correctness determines whether rule, configuration, and type-graph edits can be masked by stale ESLint diagnostics. The policy is single-sourced but trapped behind sourced shell, ambient globals, an embedded Node heredoc, and a line-oriented subprocess protocol. Tests cover current behavior and overt failures degrade safely to no cache, but the compiler cannot connect either consumer to the returned argument shape.
candidates.proposedDirection: Extract cache identity, directory selection, pruning, and argument construction into an importable TypeScript module. Let lint-agent call it directly and retain a thin shell adapter with an explicit machine protocol for eslint-main.sh.

candidates.title: Make socket rate-limit classification independent of human-readable text

evidence.note: The per-packet middleware represents rate-limit rejection only as an ordinary Error with an English message.
The error handler derives the client-facing RATE_LIMIT code by comparing err.message to that exact text.
The test named for RATE_LIMIT categorization describes the string mapping but does not assert the emitted error code.

candidates.problem: A presentation string is also an undocumented sentinel between two branches. Editing or wrapping only the producer text makes genuine throttling errors reach clients as INTERNAL_ERROR, and the existing categorization test does not inspect the emitted payload. Nothing structurally connects the rejection cause to its protocol code.
candidates.proposedDirection: Represent rate-limit rejection with a tagged or custom error, map that stable discriminator to RATE_LIMIT while keeping message text presentational, and assert the emitted error payload in a focused test.

candidates.title: Unify character-create choice chips and restore pressed-state semantics

evidence.note: Class-skill chips independently implement capped selection, disabled handling, and selected styling but expose no aria-pressed state.
Language chips repeat the interaction and style branches, again without aria-pressed.
SpellOptionButton implements the same choice-chip model but exposes isSelected through aria-pressed.

The corresponding spell-choice test asserts semantic aria-pressed state, demonstrating the drift.

candidates.problem: Three character-creation choice-chip implementations maintain selected, disabled, focus, and click semantics separately. candidates.proposedDirection: Extract a small character-create choice-chip primitive that owns aria-pressed, common focus/selection styling, disabled behavior, and click guards. Keep domain labels, cap calculations, and spell badges in callers.

candidates.title: The notification UI ignores the server cursor, making every persisted notification after the newest 20 inaccessible

evidence.note: The public list input supports an optional cursor and bounded page size.
The server counts all unread rows independently of the page and returns nextCursor when more notification rows exist.
The sole client hook issues a normal one-page query with limit 20 and never passes or consumes a cursor.
The popover renders only the hook's current array and exposes no load-more or history path.

candidates.problem: The persistence and wire layers implement notification history, but the only client fetch stops after 20 rows and discards nextCursor. After enough notifications accumulate, unreadCount can include rows the user cannot inspect or mark individually, and without a retention policy the inaccessible tail only grows.
candidates.proposedDirection: Use an infinite notification query, expose guarded load-more state in the popover, and preserve socket prepends plus optimistic mark-read updates across loaded pages. Add focused multi-page and socket-prepend coverage.

candidates.title: Debt-log variants require non-exhaustive dispatch across parsing, reporting, and accounting

evidence.note: The four-record union is not uniformly discriminated: accepted debt has no kind and needs a presence-based predicate.
The parser dispatches three explicit kinds and sends every other value, including unknown kinds, through the accepted-debt schema.
Report rendering reimplements four-way selection as an ordered type-guard ladder with a defensive fallthrough.
Lifecycle accounting separately dispatches retirement, accepted debt, metric migration, and coverage shrink through repeated predicates.
The update writer constructs each event family independently and hand-orders the heterogeneous batch.

candidates.problem: Debt-log record kinds form a persisted protocol, but classification and behavior are hand-dispatched in the parser, renderer, writer, and accounting paths. Because accepted debt lacks the common discriminator, TypeScript cannot require exhaustive handling: a new variant can be omitted or misclassified, and an unknown kind currently falls into accepted-debt validation instead of failing explicitly.
candidates.proposedDirection: Normalize legacy kind-less accepted-debt rows at parse time into a uniformly discriminated union, emit an explicit accepted-debt kind for new rows, reject unknown kinds, and convert downstream consumers to exhaustive kind switches.

origins.originalTitle: debt-log variants use several disconnected dispatch surfaces — larger and less certain than the retained metric registry finding
